text: Gleam has no arity overloading, so gleam-clj emits single-arity defns. Question for later: if we ever want compiled fns to expose Clojure multi-arity (defn f ([x]...)([x y]...)), it needs a source convention (e.g. fn-name/1, fn-name/2 sibling fns collapsed at emit) since no single Gleam construct maps to it. Today the multi-arity lives in hand-written wrapper nss, which is the right place. Revisit only if a real consumer needs variadic entry points from compiled code.
